content: 1. Both ozanimod and stat medications can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored in such cases. 2. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, ozanimod treatment should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs that have known arrhythmogenic properties. 3. Pantoprazole increases the toxicity of ozanimod through mechanisms involving other pathways. Alternative drugs should be considered or therapy should be avoided. Co-administration of ozanimod, a BCRP substrate, with BCRP inhibitors increases the exposure of both minor (RP101988, RP101075) and major active metabolites (CC112273, CC1084037) of ozanimod, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 4. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of paroxetine by enhancing sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 5. The active metabolite of ozanimod inhibits MAO-B in vitro, which may lead to serious adverse reactions, including hypertensive crisis. Co-administration of ozanimod with drugs that increase norepinephrine or serotonin is not recommended. Blood pressure should be monitored closely during concomitant use. 6. Both ozanimod and pasireotide can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 7. Ozanimod and pazopanib both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 8. Co-administration of ozanimod with immunosuppressive therapies, such as peginterferon beta-1a, may increase the risk of additive immunosuppressive effects and infection. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, the half-life and mode of action of these drugs should be considered to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 9. Both ozanimod and pentamidine increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 10. Ozanimod and pentazocine both enhance sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 11. Co-administration of ozanimod with MAO-B inhibitors may decrease the exposure of ozanimod’s active metabolites, potentially inhibiting MAO. This interaction has not been studied clinically, but the increased risk of nonselective MAO inhibition may lead to hypertensive crisis. At least 14 days should elapse between discontinuing ozanimod and initiating MAO inhibitors. 12. Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of ozanimod by inducing CYP2C8. Co-administration with strong CYP2C8 inducers reduces the exposure of ozanimod’s active metabolites (CC112273 and CC1084037), potentially decreasing its efficacy. Co-administration is not recommended. 13. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of phentermine by enhancing sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 14. Both ozanimod and procainamide increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 15. Procarbazine and ozanimod both enhance sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Ozanimod and propafenone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 17. Ozanimod and protriptyline both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Ozanimod also increases the toxicity of protriptyline by enhancing sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 18. Ozanimod increases the toxicity of pseudoephedrine by enhancing sympathetic (adrenergic) effects, such as increased blood pressure and heart rate. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 19. Both ozanimod and quetiapine increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 20. Both ozanimod and quinidine increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 21. Both ozanimod and quinine increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 22. Co-administration of ozanimod with ranolazine increases the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 23. Co-administration of ozanimod with immunosuppressive therapies, such as prednisolone or prednisone, may increase the risk of additive immunosuppressive effects and infection. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored. When switching from drugs with prolonged immune effects, the half-life and mode of action of these drugs should be considered to avoid unintended additive immunosuppressive effects. 24. Co-administration of ozanimod with vaccines, such as pneumococcal, polio, rabies, or other vaccines, may reduce vaccine efficacy due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. No clinical data are available on the efficacy and safety of vaccinations in patients taking ozanimod. Vaccinations may be less effective if co-administered with ozanimod. 25. Co-administration of ozanimod with ponatinib increases the toxicity of ozanimod by increasing the exposure of its active metabolites. Alternative drugs should be used or avoided. 26. Co-administration of ozanimod with ponesimod may increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution should be exercised, and patients should be monitored. 27. Co-administration of ozanimod with posaconazole increases the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 28. Co-administration of ozanimod with quizartinib increases the QTc interval. Patients should be monitored more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs.
